# Multi-view sequencer, harmonic popover, live jam, optional tracker

Design record of the handoff `glassloom_sequencer_views_live_jam_handoff_prompt.md` (2026-11-24, from the
client-side planning). Status: **planned, nothing built.** Work items are in `TODO.md` (thread 0h).

Glassloom is upgraded step by step into a multi-view workstation. All views are projections over one
canonical event store; no view owns notes.

## Steps and order

Strict order. Build one, verify it in the browser, then go on. Step 7 is gated.

| # | Step | One line |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Expanded view | focused track at `100vh`, chromatic multi-octave grid, piano gutter on the left |
| 2 | Waterfall view | step 1 rotated 90° clockwise: pitch on X, time falls down onto a bottom keyboard |
| 3 | Tonnetz popover | 12 pitch classes, each once; triads as triangles; draggable, non-blocking |
| 4 | Improv piano roll | free-time (tick) recording and editing on the expanded grid |
| 5 | Song <-> sequencer, loop bounds | drill down from a clip; loop in/out at song and step level |
| 6 | Play vs. edit focus | `playingPatternId` apart from `editingPatternId`; cue and launch |
| 7 | Module tracker (OPTIONAL) | FastTracker 2 style raw MIDI rows. **Not without explicit approval.** |

## Shared data model

Views never keep their own note arrays. Events are integer ticks (`TICKS_PER_STEP`, 24 or 96 per 16th):

```js
{
  id: string,
  startTick: number,      // exact, unquantized allowed
  durationTicks: number,
  note: number,           // MIDI 0..127
  velocity: number,       // 0..127
  channel: number,        // MIDI channel / instrument index
  flags: {
    accent: boolean,      // ACC
    slide: boolean,       // SLD
    gate: number,         // GATE
    probability: number,  // PROB 0..100
    nudgeTicks: number,   // NUDGE, micro offset
    seventh: boolean,     // 7TH
  },
}
```

### Rows versus arbitrary timing

- Row `r` spans `[r * TPS, (r + 1) * TPS)`. An event belongs to row `floor(startTick / TPS)` and has a
  sub-step offset `startTick - r * TPS` in `0..TPS-1`.
- Editing pitch or velocity of an existing event keeps its `startTick` and `durationTicks`.
- A new event on row `r` starts at `r * TPS` (plus an explicit offset).
- Quantize (`Q`) and humanize (`H`) run only when the user asks.
- Several events in one row (chords, rolls, overdubs) are shown as stacked voices or sub-rows, never dropped.

### Scale versus folding

Expanded views draw all 12 semitones per octave. White/black key shading shows the keys; the active scale
and root keep the amber highlight. Non-scale rows are not hidden (the compact view keeps its folding).

### Workspace state

- `viewMode`: `'compact' | 'expanded' | 'waterfall' | 'improv'` (`'tracker'` only if step 7 is approved).
- `isTonnetzOpen`: boolean, the popover floats over every view.
- `playingPatternId`, `editingPatternId`: per track or global (decision open, see below).

## Step 1: expanded view with piano gutter

- Expand button (`[⤢]`) in each track's top bar, next to `Trip` / `bar 1`.
- Pill group in the expanded header: `Grid | Waterfall | Improv | Tonnetz`.
- Keys: `F` toggles compact/expanded; `Escape` closes the Tonnetz popover first, then leaves expanded.
- Container: `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 100; display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  background: #0b0b0d`. Generator controls (`Len Root Scale Oct Follow < > -1 +1 Dice Chord Aid Trip`) stay
  docked on top.
- 3-4 octaves around `Oct`, vertical scroll. The lanes `ACC SLD GATE PROB NUDGE 7TH` go into a collapsible
  bottom drawer.
- Piano gutter, about 64 px wide, 1:1 with the grid rows: white keys full width, black keys (C# D# F# G# A#)
  60 % width on top, octave labels (`C2 C3 C4 C5`) on the C keys. Pointer-down and drag-glissando send live
  note-on/off to the track's instrument; active keys light up in `#00e5ff`.

## Step 2: waterfall view

- Grid rotated 90° clockwise: pitch on X (low to high, left to right), time on Y, falling toward the bottom.
- Horizontal piano docked at the bottom (88-120 px), 1:1 with the pitch lanes.
- Falling bars and active keys in `#00e5ff` / `#eab308` when they cross the strike line. Cells can be
  toggled by click; the bottom keys can be played.

## Step 3: non-repeating Tonnetz popover

- Strictly 12 nodes, each pitch class once (no infinite lattice). Arranged along fifths (+7) and thirds
  (+4 / +3) with wrap-around markers, so major and minor triads are selectable triangles without duplicate
  nodes.
- Opens by the `Tonnetz` button or `T`; floating, draggable, non-blocking, about 300 x 280 px.
- A node click triggers or inserts the pitch; a triangle click triggers or inserts the chord and shows its
  name. Highlights follow playback and scale.
- Related: the Chord chip and Tonnetz picker (`step.chord`) already exist; see where the popover can reuse
  `app/lattice.js`.

## Step 4: improv piano roll

- Continuous note bars (`startTick`, `durationTicks`, velocity) on the multi-octave grid.
- Controls: `Rec` (`R`), `Overdub` / `Replace`, `Loop Length`, `Quantize` (`Off`, `1/16`, `1/8`, `Triplet`).
- Input: WebMIDI, QWERTY, on-screen piano, Tonnetz; timed against the transport clock, drawn as the playhead
  moves.
- Edit: drag a body for pitch/time, drag the right edge for duration, create/delete, velocity lane at the
  bottom.

## Step 5: song <-> sequencer, loop boundaries

- Double-click a clip, or `Enter` on a selected clip, opens that pattern in the active sequencer view,
  pre-scrolled to its pitch range.
- Breadcrumb on top (`Song > Bars 5-8 > ORGAN 8 [Pat 2]`); `Escape` goes back to Song with scroll and zoom
  kept.
- Song ruler: draggable `Loop Start` / `Loop End` (`I` set in, `O` set out, `L` toggle loop).
- Step ruler: synced sub-loop handles, so e.g. steps 9-16 inside `Len 16` can loop while editing.
- Exists today: the LOOP chip on the transport (1/2/4/8 bars) and `app/song-view.js`; the new bounds
  have to agree with them.

## Step 6: play versus edit focus

- `playingPatternId` feeds the scheduler (badge `PLAY`, `#eab308` / `#22c55e`). `editingPatternId` feeds the
  editor (badge/border `EDIT`, `#00e5ff`).
- `Lock / Cue` toggle (`C`): Locked, selecting a pattern moves both pointers. Cue, selecting an unplayed
  pattern opens it for quiet editing while the playing one continues.
- `Launch` (`Space`) queues `editingPatternId` into `playingPatternId` at the next bar or loop boundary.
  Optional cue/monitor preview that does not disturb the live output.

## Step 7 (optional, approval gate): module tracker

**Do not build or wire without the user's explicit request in a later message.** If asked, on the tick store:

- Vertical rows `00..Len-1` (hex/decimal toggle), centered on the playhead with `Follow`.
- Columns: `ROW`, `NOTE` (`C-4`, `A#4`, `===` off, `---` empty), `CH` (`01`-`10`), `VEL` (hex `00`-`7F`,
  linked to ACC), `FX`/`DLY` (`Gxx` slide, `Lxx` gate, `Pxx` probability, `Cxx` CC, `Dxx` sub-step tick
  delay so unquantized note-ons stay visible and intact).
- Optional `Raw Hex` column or inspector with the outgoing bytes (`90 3C 64`, `80 3C 00`, `B0 41 7F`);
  QWERTY note entry, hex digit entry, step-skip navigation.

## Rules for all steps

1. Strict order; verify each step before the next. No step 7 without approval.
2. Switching views and editing loses nothing: notes, `startTick`/`durationTicks`, scale/root/octave, lanes.
3. Look: dark theme, 1 px borders, tabular/monospace readouts, `#00e5ff` active/edit, `#eab308` scale/play.
   Colours come from `app/look.js`, not literals (project rule).
4. Keyboard safety: the single-key shortcuts (`F T R L I O C Space`) are ignored while an `input`, `select`,
   `textarea` or `contentEditable` has focus.

## Open questions (to settle before step 1)

- **Store.** The handoff wants a tick-based event store; `app/store.js` today is step-based (steps, per-step
  values). Is the tick store a new layer under it, a migration, or a view over it? Saved songs and presets
  (`app/presets/*.data.js`) must still load. Decide before step 4; step 1-3 can run on the step store.
- **Compat of the handoff's names.** `viewMode`, `playingPatternId`, `editingPatternId` are names from the
  handoff; map them to the real pattern ids in `store.js` and `song-view.js`.
- **Pointers per track or global** (step 6).
- **Tryout.** Which tryout (number) carries these views and which client questions they answer; develop in
  `/dev/` first (CLAUDE.md, Tryouts).
- **Pi 5 frame budget** for the waterfall's falling bars (pre-rendered sprites, measure).
- **Touch.** The target is a transparent touchscreen: the `F`, `T`, `Escape` shortcuts need on-screen
  buttons too.
